verses.text: At the end of every seven years, you must cancel all debts.

This is how it must be done: everyone who has lent money to a fellow Israelite must cancel the debt. He must not demand payment from his neighbour or his relative, because the LORD's time for cancelling debts has been announced.
You may demand payment from a foreigner, but you must cancel any debt your fellow Israelite owes you.
There should be no poor people among you, for the LORD will greatly bless you in the land the LORD your God is giving you to own as your share,
if only you carefully obey the LORD your God and are careful to keep all these commands I am giving you today.
For the LORD your God will bless you as he promised. You will lend money to many nations, but you will not need to borrow. You will rule over many nations, but they will not rule over you.
If there is a poor person among your fellow Israelites in any of the towns of the land the LORD your God is giving you, do not be hard-hearted or tight-fisted toward that poor person.
Instead, be open-handed and freely lend them whatever they need.

Be careful not to have this wicked thought in your heart: "The seventh year, the year for cancelling debts, is near." Do not look unkindly at your poor fellow Israelite and give them nothing. They may cry out to the LORD against you, and you will be guilty of sin.
Give generously to them, and do not be unhappy about giving. Because of this, the LORD your God will bless you in all your work and in everything you do.
There will always be poor people in the land. That is why I command you to be open-handed toward your fellow Israelites who are poor and in need in your land.
If one of your fellow Hebrews, a man or a woman, is sold to you and serves you for six years, you must set them free in the seventh year.
And when you set them free, do not send them away empty-handed.
Give to them generously from your flock, your threshing floor, and your winepress. Give to them as the LORD your God has blessed you.
Remember that you were slaves in Egypt and the LORD your God set you free. That is why I am giving you this command today.
But your servant may say to you, "I do not want to leave you," because he loves you and your family and is happy with you.
Then take a sharp tool and push it through his ear lobe into the door, and he will be your servant for life. Do the same for your female servant.
Do not think it is hard to set your servant free, because their six years of service have been worth twice as much as a hired worker. And the LORD your God will bless you in everything you do.
Set apart for the LORD your God every firstborn male of your herds and flocks. Do not put the firstborn of your cattle to work, and do not cut the wool of the firstborn of your sheep.
Each year you and your family must eat them in the presence of the LORD your God at the place he will choose.
If an animal has a defect, if it is lame or blind or has any other serious defect, do not sacrifice it to the LORD your God.
Eat it in your own towns. Both people who are unclean and people who are clean may eat it, as they would eat gazelle or deer.
But you must not eat the blood. Pour it out on the ground like water.
